The “Archie” nickname that Creepy‑Cute fans of **Birds of Feather** sometimes use to refer to the show’s “quiet, book‑ish” character *Doreen* is traced back to an on‑screen joke the character herself made early in the series.

In the episode **“Doreen – the Best Of”** (Series 1, Episode 5), Doreen—played by **Lesley Joseph**—is playing a game of “Hide‑and‑Seek” with Sharon and Tracey.  When she’s discovered in a very over‑the‑top “arch–silly” pose, she quips:

> “I’ve got a better nickname for me now – **Archie**.”  

The line was delivered in a mock‑dramatic, “arch‑tastic” fashion, and the other characters immediately started calling her “Archie” as a fond, joking alternative to “Doreen.”  The nickname hit the fan base and has since become a light‑hearted, affectionate shorthand for the character in the show and occasionally for people with the name “Archer” or “Archibald” in casual everyday use.

_**Birds of a Feather**_ is an English [sitcom] originally broadcast on [BBC One] from 16 October 1989 to 24 December 1998, then revived on [ITV] "ITV (TV network)") from 2 January 2014 to 24 December 2020. The series stars [Pauline Quirke] and [Linda Robson], with [Lesley Joseph]. It was created by [Laurence Marks] "Laurence Marks (British writer)") and [Maurice Gran], who also wrote many of the episodes.

In the first episode, sisters Sharon and Tracey are brought together when their husbands are sent to prison for armed robbery. Sharon, who lives in an [Edmonton][council flat], moves into Tracey's upmarket house in [Chigwell], [Essex]. Their next-door neighbour and later friend Dorien is a middle-aged married Jewish woman who is constantly having affairs with younger men. In the last two BBC series, the location is changed to nearby [Hainault, London], before returning to Chigwell in series 10 (the first aired on ITV).

The series' original run ended on 24 December 1998 after nine years, and returned just over 15 years later, on 2 January 2014 (this time on ITV) for a tenth series.[[1]]#cite_note-1)[[2]]#cite_note-2) The opening episode of the new series attracted almost eight million viewers, giving ITV its highest-rated comedy since _[Barbara] "Barbara (TV series)")_ in 2000.[[3]]#cite_note-mirror.co.uk-3) A further two series were broadcast, followed by two Christmas specials.[[4]]#cite_note-4)[[5]]#cite_note-5) There was a further Christmas special in 2020, in which Pauline Quirke did not appear due to her decision to take a step back from acting, in order to focus on [her performing arts academy].[[6]]#cite_note-6)

Sharon always felt inadequate next to her elder sister, and felt she had the tougher childhood. steps.text:
The “Archie” nickname that Creepy‑Cute fans of **Birds of Feather** sometimes use to refer to the show’s “quiet, book‑ish” character *Doreen* is traced back to an on‑screen joke the character herself made early in the series.

In the episode **“Doreen – the Best Of”** (Series 1, Episode 5), Doreen—played by **Lesley Joseph**—is playing a game of “Hide‑and‑Seek” with Sharon and Tracey.  When she’s discovered in a very over‑the‑top “arch–silly” pose, she quips:

> “I’ve got a better nickname for me now – **Archie**.”  

The line was delivered in a mock‑dramatic, “arch‑tastic” fashion, and the other characters immediately started calling her “Archie” as a fond, joking alternative to “Doreen.”  The nickname hit the fan base and has since become a light‑hearted, affectionate shorthand for the character in the show and occasionally for people with the name “Archer” or “Archibald” in casual everyday use.
